cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster with stringed instruments. David is talking straight to the LORD, and friend, this is not a happy little tune. He opens with, "O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath."

cards.question: David keeps going with his next request. What does he ask the LORD to show him?
David tells the LORD he's strong enough to get through this on his own.

cards.text: David says he's frail and his bones are in agony. And it goes deeper than his bones, friend, because his soul is deeply distressed.

cards.question: In the middle of all that pain, David asks the LORD the same question twice in a row. What is it?

cards.text: Then David asks the LORD to turn, deliver his soul and save him. No fancy speech, no plan B. Just a man reaching for the only One who can actually help.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to save him. What reason does David give?

cards.text: David gives the LORD one more reason to save him. And this one has to do with death.

cards.question: David says the dead in Sheol keep right on praising the LORD.

cards.text: Now David tells the LORD he's weary from groaning. Friend, when even the GROANING wears you out, you are TIRED.

cards.question: David says his tears dry up fast and he sleeps through the night.

cards.text: All night he floods his bed with weeping and drenches his couch with tears. That pillow doesn't need a towel, friend. That couch needs a LIFEGUARD.

cards.question: David says his eyes fail from grief. They grow dim because of all his ___.

cards.text: Then the whole song FLIPS. The same David who was drenching his couch turns around and tells all the workers of iniquity to depart from him.

cards.question: David suddenly tells the workers of iniquity to get away from him. What does he say has changed?

answers.text: The LORD has heard his weeping
His tears have finally dried up
His army has just shown up

cards.question: David says it again another way: "The LORD has heard my cry for ___."

cards.text: And David says the LORD accepts his prayer. Friend, I KNOW that switch: years in the dark of a junk drawer, and then one night the light pours in.

cards.question: Now David looks at all his enemies. What does he say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will turn back in disgrace
They will win in the end

cards.text: His enemies will be ashamed and dismayed, turning back in sudden disgrace like somebody who just walked into the wrong meeting. The man who started this song drenching his couch ends it sure the LORD has heard him.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 16 quotes "The LORD has heard my cry for ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to supply the exact words David repeats ('How long'). The wrong answers 'Why me' and 'Where are You' are other possible wordings. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out which words David used, so this tests wording rather than movement or meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then David asks…', 'No fancy speech, no plan B.' and 'Just a man reaching…'. Only the opening card may run to three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'All night he floods…', 'That pillow doesn't need a towel, friend.' and 'That couch needs a LIFEGUARD.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks what makes David's eyes grow dim ('foes'). No earlier card mentions enemies or foes, so the baker can't reason from 'foes' over 'years' or 'sins'. The only way to get it right is luck, or guessing the next word of the line.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card says David 'started this song drenching his couch'. The psalm starts with a plea not to be rebuked in anger (6:1). The couch drenching comes in 6:6.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card cites only Psalm 6:10, but its second sentence uses 6:6 (drenching his couch) and 6:8-9 (the LORD has heard him).

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The second sentence ('The man who started this song… ends it sure the LORD has heard him') sums up the whole psalm instead of moving it forward.
